record.original_question: Let F : R^2 -> R^2 be a smooth map with a fixed point such that the spectral radius of |DF(x)| is strictly less than 1 for every x in R^2. Must that fixed point be globally asymptotically stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Let F : R^2 -> R^2 be a smooth map having a fixed point and such that rho(|DF(x)|) < 1, for all x in R^2. Is it true that the fixed point is globally asymptotically stable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth map possessing a fixed point $p\in\mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., $F(p)=p$). For each $x\in\mathbb{R}^2$, let $DF(x)$ denote the Jacobian matrix of $F$ at $x$, let $|DF(x)|$ denote the $2\times 2$ matrix obtained from $DF(x)$ by replacing each entry by its absolute value, and let $\rho(\cdot)$ denote the spectral radius (the maximum modulus of eigenvalues) of a square matrix. Assume that
$$\rho(|DF(x)|) < 1 \qquad \text{for every } x\in\mathbb{R}^2.$$
Question: Must the fixed point $p$ be globally asymptotically stable for the discrete dynamical system $x_{n+1}=F(x_n)$? That is, must $p$ be a Lyapunov-stable fixed point such that $\lim_{n\to\infty}F^n(x)=p$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a planar discrete global asymptotic stability problem of Markus–Yamabe / LaSalle type, using the entry-wise absolute-value Jacobian and its spectral radius. It appears in lists of open problems on low-dimensional dynamical systems and on LaSalle's problems; while related discrete Markus–Yamabe results are known (the discrete Markus–Yamabe conjecture holds for planar polynomial maps but fails in higher dimensions), no resolution of this specific entry-wise variant in dimension two has been located.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: A list of problems on planar differential equations, difference equations, global asymptotic stability and related topics, posed as open questions worth investigating.
status_evidence.claim: This and related discrete planar global stability questions are listed among open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems.

status_evidence.title: A note on LaSalle's problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses LaSalle-type problems on global asymptotic stability of discrete dynamical systems under Jacobian conditions.
status_evidence.claim: LaSalle-type questions on discrete global asymptotic stability under Jacobian spectral conditions remain a subject of investigation.

status_evidence.title: Markus–Yamabe conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The discrete Markus–Yamabe conjecture is true for planar polynomial maps but counterexamples exist in higher dimensions and beyond the polynomial setting.
status_evidence.claim: Discrete global stability under spectral conditions on the Jacobian is delicate and not generally true; planar smooth versions remain a focus of open questions.
